value.body: An interpreter carries spoken meaning between two languages as people talk — at business meetings, factory visits by foreign partners, trade fairs, conferences, hospitals and courts. Much of the work is freelance and assignment-based, with some in-house roles at companies that work closely with foreign partners.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.A. or M.A. in a foreign language

items.label: Foreign tourist arrivals
items.note: Rose to roughly 97–100 lakh in 2024; sources differ

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most start with short escort or business-meeting assignments through agencies, alongside translation work. Conference-level simultaneous interpreting usually needs further training and years of practice.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: High spoken fluency in both languages

value.title: At a glance
items: Work comes in bursts around events and business visits.
Japanese, German, French, Korean and Chinese interpreters are hired where those countries' firms operate.
Many interpreters also take translation work between assignments.

competition.note: BA (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
